title: Unit – 1 : Session – 8 | Natural Acceptance
sections: Q1. NATURAL ACCEPTANCE is the innate, constant acceptance in the Self for what is right and harmonious — it needs no external proof. It differs from LIKING/APPEAL: liking is conditioned, changeable and varies from person to person (taste in food, fashion), while natural acceptance is the same for everyone, at all times, in all places. Example: respect in relationship is naturally acceptable to every human being, whereas one may 'like' or dislike a particular greeting style.

Q2. NAMASTE example: the FEELING behind Namaste — respect for the other — is naturally acceptable to everyone, always. The FORM (folded hands) is a cultural expression: naturally acceptable where understood, possibly not where unfamiliar. WHAT CAN be checked by natural acceptance: the intention/feeling (Is respect acceptable to me? — yes, always). WHAT CANNOT be decided by natural acceptance alone: the external form, custom or ritual — these are matters of tradition and choice. Natural acceptance validates content, not customs.

Q3. NATURAL ACCEPTANCE: arises from within the Self, constant, universal, unconditional — e.g., acceptance of trust. ACCEPTANCE: agreeing to something after reasoning, influence or convention — it can change with new information or social change. FORCED ACCEPTANCE: submission under pressure, fear or greed — against one's inner acceptance, producing contradiction and unhappiness. Only natural acceptance gives definite, harmonious conduct; acceptance is provisional; forced acceptance is unstable and breeds resentment.
